ai.title: Enhanced API error messages with endpoint context
ai.summary: API client now throws errors including method and URL for non-retryable failures. Timeout errors in agent-runtime now specify the endpoint and duration. Affects `cli/src/utils/codebuff-api.ts` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/llm-api/codebuff-web-api.ts`. Error objects preserve original name and cause via enhanced error wrapping.

eli5.text: When the assistant can't reach its connected services, it now reports exactly which service call failed and where, instead of a vague error. If you ever see a failure message while using the CLI, you will notice it now mentions the specific endpoint and method that timed out or was unreachable. This update is live today and only affects people running the CLI tool.

ai.title: Fix Claude OAuth error detection via APICallError status
ai.summary: getErrorStatusCode now checks both statusCode and status properties to handle AI SDK APICallError conventions. isClaudeOAuthRateLimitError and isClaudeOAuthAuthError use this helper to correctly detect 429, 401, and 403 responses from Claude OAuth. Covers sdk/src/error-utils.ts and sdk/src/impl/llm.ts. Prevents missed rate-limit and auth handling when the AI SDK uses status instead of statusCode.

eli5.text: When you use Claude through an AI coding helper, the tool sometimes failed to notice when your request was rate-limited (too many requests) or rejected by Claude's login system. Now it checks both common places where the error code can appear, so it correctly detects these limits and login issues and handles them properly instead of missing them.

ai.title: CLI agent factory extracted to modular files
ai.summary: CLI agent definitions in .agents/ now call createCliAgent() from .agents/lib/create-cli-agent.ts instead of duplicating inline config. Prompts, schemas, and types split into cli-agent-prompts.ts, cli-agent-schemas.ts, cli-agent-types.ts. Covers claude-code-cli.ts, codebuff-local-cli.ts, codex-cli.ts, gemini-cli.ts. Factory accepts cliName, shortName, startCommand, permissionNote, spawnerPromptExtras.

eli5.text: The four command-line testing helpers for Claude Code, Codebuff, Codex, and Gemini now pull their shared setup from one central place instead of each carrying around a long copy of the same instructions and rules. If you looked, each helper file would be much shorter and the common prompts and validation rules would live together in dedicated spots, so adding or changing something across all four only happens once. This is already live: anyone triggering automated CLI tests or code reviews now relies on that single shared setup.

ai.title: CLI: process queued messages one at a time
ai.summary: The CLI message queue now enforces sequential processing via `isProcessingQueueRef` in `use-message-queue.ts`, replacing the previous timeout-based dispatch. This prevents race conditions where multiple messages could be sent concurrently if the queue drained faster than the agent could respond. The change spans `cli/src/hooks/use-message-queue.ts`, `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts`, and `cli/src/utils/yield-to-event-loop.ts` (new file). `sendMessage` now returns a `Promise<void>`, and `finalizeQueueState` in `send-message.ts` handles lock release on completion, abort, or error.

eli5.text: When you send the CLI multiple messages in quick succession, it now waits for each one to finish before starting the next, instead of potentially mixing them up. This prevents confusing or overlapping responses when the agent takes a turn and you queue up more input during that turn. You won't notice anything when typing normally, but if you paste several prompts back-to-back, they'll arrive in clean, separate turns rather than jumbled together.

ai.title: Add block-processor utilities to CLI
ai.summary: New `cli/src/utils/block-processor.ts` exports `processBlocks` and `BlockProcessorHandlers` to abstract content block iteration. Groups consecutive reasoning, tool, agent, and implementor blocks via `implementor-helpers` and `chat` types. Internal refactor for `BlocksRenderer` and `AgentBody` in the CLI surface.

eli5.text: When you run a CLI command that displays a conversation, the program now processes each type of message block (like reasoning, tool calls, or agent responses) through one centralized utility that groups consecutive blocks of the same kind before passing them to the display layer. This means you will see reasoning blocks streamed together, tool calls batched as a group, and agent responses rendered according to each handler, instead of each individual message fragment triggering a separate render call. The change is internal to the CLI and does not alter what you see on screen; it just cleans up how the rendering code repeats itself between the BlocksRenderer and AgentBody components.

ai.title: Add useGridLayout hook for CLI responsive layout
ai.summary: New `useGridLayout` hook in `cli/src/hooks/use-grid-layout.ts` computes responsive grid dimensions based on available width. It uses thresholds (100, 150, 200 chars) to determine max columns, then delegates to `computeSmartColumns` from `layout-helpers` to finalize column count and width. The hook returns a memoized object containing `columns`, `columnWidth`, and `columnGroups` (items distributed round-robin). This provides a standardized mechanism for CLI components to adapt their layout to terminal width changes.

eli5.text: When the command-line tool displays information that is normally spread across columns, it now checks how wide your terminal window is and automatically rearranges that information into fewer or more columns so it fits without getting cut off. The arrangement is worked out from a few width marks (around 100, 150, and 200 characters), and each piece of information is shifted into the next column in turn, so widening or narrowing the window immediately lines everything up again without you having to do anything. This new behavior is already live for the command-line tool.

ai.title: CLI implementor-helpers gains generic block grouping
ai.summary: cli/src/utils/implementor-helpers.ts adds generic groupConsecutiveBlocks and derives groupConsecutiveImplementors, groupConsecutiveNonImplementorAgents, groupConsecutiveToolBlocks. PROPOSED_EDIT_TOOL_NAMES now derives from EDIT_TOOL_NAMES via map. Removes JSDoc on most exports. Scope: cli/src/utils only.

eli5.text: The CLI’s helper code that organizes assistant messages now uses one flexible grouping routine instead of separate ones for each case. It can collect runs of implementor agents, runs of non-implementor agents, and runs of tool calls through a single shared mechanism, and add-tool names are derived from base edit names rather than listed separately. You wouldn’t see this directly, but the underlying message handling is tidier and easier to maintain as a result. The JSDoc comments on most exports were also removed during the cleanup.

ai.title: Add GridLayout and ErrorBoundary CLI components
ai.summary: New `GridLayout` and `ErrorBoundary` components added to `cli/src/components`. `GridLayout` renders responsive multi-column layouts using `useGridLayout`, while `ErrorBoundary` provides a structural wrapper for error fallbacks. Scope limited to CLI UI subsystem. `ErrorBoundary` uses a `memo` wrapper due to OpenTUI's lack of class component support, delegating true error catching to `withErrorFallback` or parent boundaries.

eli5.text: The command-line version of the tool gained two building blocks for organizing what you see on screen. A new grid layout helper arranges items into columns that shrink or expand based on available space, so lists and buttons can flow side-by-side on wide screens or stack into a single column on narrow ones. A paired error-boundary helper acts as a placeholder container that can swap in a backup message or view if the content it holds fails to render. These pieces are now present on disk and in the test suite but sit inside the interface layer, so you would only notice them if a future screen is built using them; the layout itself already reacts to window width, while the error boundary today mainly reserves space for parent components to plug in real fallback behavior later.

ai.title: Add AgentBlockGrid and ToolBlockGroup CLI components
ai.summary: New `AgentBlockGrid` renders multiple agent branches in a grid with a dynamic status footer (running, failed, completed counts). `ToolBlockGroup` wraps consecutive `ToolBranch` components, applying conditional vertical spacing based on adjacent timeline blocks. These components reside in `cli/src/components/` and handle layout logic previously scattered or absent in the CLI renderer.

eli5.text: The chat window you see now lines up multiple conversation threads in a tidy grid instead of a single stacked column, and it shows a quick summary at the bottom telling you how many threads are still running, how many finished, and how many hit an error. When several tool calls happen back-to-back, they now group together with just the right amount of space between them so the timeline stays easy to follow. If you look, each thread still scrolls and updates live, but the overall page feels more organized, like browser tabs in a row rather than a long list.

ai.title: Decompose CLI block rendering into dedicated components
ai.summary: Refactored CLI message rendering by splitting monolithic block logic into `cli/src/components/blocks/`. New files `agent-branch-wrapper.tsx`, `blocks-renderer.tsx`, `single-block.tsx`, `user-content-copy.tsx`, and `block-helpers.ts` handle specific rendering tasks. Existing components like `agent-block-grid.tsx` and `implementor-row.tsx` moved into the `blocks/` directory with updated import paths. This modularization improves maintainability of the CLI UI layer.

eli5.text: If you run the CLI and a conversation message contains agentic work, its on-screen layout is now assembled from smaller, single-purpose pieces instead of one big chunk of code. The visible result for you is the same today: the same blocks (message grid, tool calls, thinking, user content) still render in the same order and style. This is purely behind-the-scenes reorganization so the code that draws those blocks is easier for the team to maintain; no access, plans, or features changed, and nothing is live that wasn't already live.

ai.title: Add UserErrorBanner component
ai.summary: New `UserErrorBanner` component added to `cli/src/components/user-error-banner.tsx` for displaying runtime errors in the CLI UI. Uses theme-aware styling with `theme.error` border and text color, and supports optional `title` prop defaulting to 'Error'. Returns `null` for empty or whitespace-only error strings. Scope limited to CLI surface.

eli5.text: When the CLI program hits a problem while running, you'll now see a clear error message in a red-bordered box at the top of your screen, instead of a plain text error. The program automatically hides any error messages that are blank or just spaces, and the error text uses your chosen color theme so it matches the rest of the interface. This only affects what you see on your screen while using the command-line tool; it doesn't change how the program behaves or what it sends to the AI.

ai.title: Fix CLI @ menu with apostrophes, preserve input, keep leading
ai.summary: CLI @ menu ignores single quotes as delimiters, enabling mentions after apostrophes. AskUserBridge stops clearing input on submit/skip, preserving user text. Terminal output and top banner preserve leading whitespace via `trimEnd` instead of `trim`. Error handling simplifies to direct `setError` without `createErrorMessage` wrapper.

eli5.text: When you type an @ sign in the command-line assistant to tag someone or something, it now works even if the word before it ends in an apostrophe (like typing "Bob's" then @name), instead of ignoring the mention. If the assistant pops up a follow-up question while you're typing and you answer or skip it, your original text stays in the box instead of being wiped out. Text the assistant shows you, like command output and the top status bar, now keeps any important spacing at the start of the lines, so things like indented lists or tree diagrams line up correctly. This is live today for everyone using the command-line version.

ai.title: CLI: extract message-block internals and wire up parallel agent
ai.summary: Refactored CLI components by extracting message-block internals into dedicated files like `blocks-renderer.tsx` and `user-content-copy.tsx`. Implemented a `GridLayout` and `useGridLayout` hook to render parallel agent children side-by-side in `message-with-agents.tsx`. Added `userError` prop to `MessageBlock` for UI-only error banners. Scope covers `cli/src/components` and `cli/src/types/chat.ts`.

eli5.text: When multiple AI agents work on the same task in the CLI, you can now see their outputs side-by-side in a clean grid layout instead of stacked vertically. The internal code that builds message displays was also reorganized into smaller, dedicated files, and the system now tracks UI-only error messages that show up as banners without affecting the actual AI response. This reorganization is already live and makes managing parallel agent work smoother in your terminal.
